doc.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021

title: Chord thinking, Stan Kenton, and playing 'Barbara Monk'
summary: Blake thinks in triad progressions, then plays his piece for Barbara Monk and recalls her.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: But the bit you played, like you reach out to the piano on occasion during this interview and you put your hands down, I’m wondering if you put a chord type to what you’re playing. Oh here’s a D flat 13 chord. Do you think that way?

No I can’t say I never — I mean well even in teaching I think more of triad progressions going to different keys rather than, I love the three years, there are three great years in Stan Kenton’s life from ’48 to ’51 or 2 and then the awful trash that came — so those have skyscraper chords but I just hear things. Would you like me to play a standard or one of my own pieces, or do we have time? We’re about to close maybe in five or ten minutes.
Yeah. I would love to hear, actually I’d love to hear something of your own, if you’d like to play, yeah, I would really enjoy that.

And of course I don’t usually play this so briefly but immediately and of course the lights are on, I’m with Monk Rowe, Aaron’s here, my wonderful cat DekTor Dutra! on my right, but that was “Barbara Monk.” Sometimes I pop to other Monk songs but this is the memory of Barbara, Toots, Nellie, Thelonious, Nica, Charlie Rouse, so many people that love Monk.
You’re very into dynamics and setting up expectations and sometimes giving us what we might expect and then sometimes not. I especially like the part where it sort of eased into that nice waltz.

Yes. I saw her waltzing almost on ice in Central Park and of course as the memories go on I sense I’m there watching her for ten minutes and of course this is exaggeration but I remember a Thanksgiving turkey supper I took her out to because her mother made wonderful organic food, but I don’t think meat was encouraged. Monk, it’s so great to be with you. I’ve loved your show for years. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
